subject.title: fix(sms): ack rate-limited Twilio callbacks instead of dropping them [AI]

question: Should a validated SMS callback above OpenClaw's dispatch quota remain an observable failure eligible for Twilio fallback or retry, or may OpenClaw return 200 while intentionally discarding it?
rationale: Current documentation and provider semantics treat non-2xx as the recovery signal, while this PR redefines 200 as successful receipt without processing; automation cannot choose that message-delivery contract.

options.title: Require admission before success
options.body: Keep HTTP 429 unless the callback is durably queued or otherwise guaranteed eventual processing before returning 2xx.

options.title: Accept intentional discard
options.body: Return 200 without dispatch only if maintainers explicitly accept irreversible overflow loss and document that fallback and retries will not run.

options.title: Pause this change
options.body: Leave the existing rejection behavior in place until a bounded durable-overflow design is available.

recommendation.title: Require admission before success
recommendation.body: Keep HTTP 429 unless the callback is durably queued or otherwise guaranteed eventual processing before returning 2xx.

likelyOwner.reason: The original SMS channel and webhook contract appear to originate from their merged feature work.
